title: Nintendo Called the Wii 'Revolution' for Two Years
hook: On April 27, 2006 Nintendo dropped the name Revolution and announced the Wii, and the internet spent the day making puns. Twenty years and 100 million consoles later, did you ever own one?
script: Did you know Nintendo spent about two years calling the Wii the Revolution? Nintendo first described its next console under the codename Revolution at E3 in two thousand four. It showed the machine itself at E3 the next year, still carrying that name. Then on April twenty seventh, two thousand six, about a month before E3, Nintendo announced the real name. Wii, spelled W, i, i. The company explained that Wii sounds like we, which emphasized that the console was for everyone. The double i spelling stood for the unique controllers and for people gathering to play. The internet was not kind. Engadget posted a list of puns the same day. GamesRadar wrote that the planet had expressed confusion or bitter hatred over the name. Nintendo did not budge. The Wii launched in North America on November nineteenth, two thousand six, with Wii Sports in the box. It went on to sell more than one hundred million consoles. The name everyone laughed at became one of the most recognized brands in gaming. This week the Wii turned twenty, and outlets like Nintendo Life and VGC marked the anniversary with best of lists. Did you ever own a Wii? Follow for more gaming history.
